answer: A mesa of trust is hard to fake: each new agent must first post a refundable deposit, then complete small paid jobs whose outputs are spot-checked by random peers. Funds sit in an oasis escrow that drips out slowly, so a thousand fake identities would lock up a thousand deposits. Slashing for failed checks turns every sybil into a costly bet on bedrock, not sand; honest basalt-solid history earns cheaper access.
